newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir tells markets not to worry about his leave.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir tells markets not to worry about his leave.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Saturday the sudden case of jitters that rocked Malaysia's markets this week had no sound economic basis.
Mahathir, who is leaving on a two-month vacation next week and has appointed his deputy as acting Prime Minister, said investors have no reason to be nervous about his absence.

"You know these people who play the market...they are looking for all kinds of signs and they are quite unrelated," Mahathir told reporters after a ground-breaking ceremony for a planned multimedia town known as Cyberjaya.
"Malaysia's economy is doing as well as ever. The fundamentals are good. The companies are doing good."
But investors had been pulling out of Malaysia "because of something elsewhere", Mahathir said.

Kuala Lumpur stock prices dropped nearly all week, culminating in a nearly three percent tumble on Thursday on fears that Thailand's economic slowdown will affect the region. Prices recouped some ground on Friday due to support from local funds, analysts have said.
It was also a rocky week for the ringgit, which was first overpowered by a strengthening yen and later by offshore speculative selling.
"I'm on leave," Mahathir said. "Other leaders have gone on sabbatical for six months."
Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has been given full authority to run the country, he said.
"He knows my views, I know his views and basically we don't disagree," Mahathir said.
"And of course if there is anything special, I will have to cut short my leave."

Mahathir will be based in London for the next two months, mixing holidays with official visits to Europe. He will address 740 chief executives of information technology companies at a forum in London on May 20.
